headline: Hacker wipes Romania's land registry database after failed extortion attempt
summary: The breach has brought Romania's entire real-estate market to a standstill, with official apps and websites offline for a week and critical services impacted.
details: A hacker breached Romania's National Agency for Cadastre and Real Estate Advertising (ANCPI) and wiped the country's entire land registry database. This devastating act followed a failed extortion attempt by the perpetrator.

The incident has paralyzed Romania's real-estate market, with official ANCPI apps and websites remaining offline for over a week. Notaries are unable to record new transactions, and citizens cannot obtain essential proof of ownership or detailed land records.

Sources indicate the hacker gained access using valid credentials, then mapped internal systems before deleting data and backups. On July 15, some stolen data, including employee credentials and internal documents, was posted for sale on a hacking forum.

Officials have since restored their website and are rebuilding the agency's entire network from scratch. Despite the hacker's claims of deleting backups, the agency appears to have had an offline copy, preventing an even more severe long-term crisis.

The stolen data was posted by "ByteToBreach," a known hacker previously linked to breaches of Sweden's e-government portal and other high-profile agencies. Security firm KELA has since identified the hacker as Zakaria Mahdjoub from Oran, Algeria.
Romania is not alone, joining Poland, Slovakia, Greece, Morocco, Russia, and Ukraine, which have also experienced hacks targeting their land registry agencies in the past three years.

headline_marked: [[Microsoft to deploy AMD Helios AI accelerators]] at scale on Azure
headline: Microsoft to deploy AMD Helios AI accelerators at scale on Azure
summary: Microsoft is adding AMD's Helios rack-scale AI accelerator to Azure, featuring Radeon Instinct MI455X GPUs and Epyc Venice CPUs, to power frontier-model AI workloads for its customers.
details: Microsoft and AMD have announced a major partnership, with Microsoft committing to deploy AMD's Helios rack-scale AI accelerator in volume on Azure. This infrastructure will power frontier-model AI workloads for both internal use and Azure AI infrastructure customers and services.

The Helios system will feature 72 next-generation Instinct MI455X GPUs, offering an aggregate of 31.1TB of HBM4 memory capacity. These GPUs provide up to 1.4 exaFLOPS of FP8 compute and 2.9 exaFLOPS of FP4 for AI models.

AMD targets 260 TB/s of scale-up bandwidth within the rack, on par with Nvidia’s Vera Rubin NVL72 system. It also aims for 43 TB/s of scale-out bandwidth using UALink over Ethernet, potentially doubling Vera Rubin's performance.

Azure will also integrate two new VM series built on AMD's upcoming sixth-gen Epyc Venice CPUs: the HDv2 series for agentic AI and data pipelines, and the HXv2 for semiconductor design workflows. Microsoft will further leverage its existing AMD Pensando DPUs to accelerate networking and storage in Azure Boost offerings.
